decision: routed to the figure-it-out playbook instead of the Feature playbook
why: this is a large cross-cutting change: six screens, an ARKit pipeline, a reminder state machine, a logger, a simulation harness, tests and a device install

decision: defined done as a device-installable app driven by a scripted scenario, plus green state-machine tests and a per-screen screenshot set
why: done has to be checkable against the real artifact, not a proxy

decision: committed the scaffold to main and pushed before any feature code
why: the brief asks for the scaffold on main first, and a reviewer needs the base to exist

decision: proved the unit-test target runs green before writing feature code
why: verification harness before features, so a later break is localizable to the unit that caused it

decision: froze the domain declarations and gave the implementation to one owner
why: four parallel implementers need one compiled contract first; declarations are identical in every slice

decision: built the current tree for the physical device to prove free-team provisioning early
why: signing and provisioning are the slowest unknown on the critical path

decision: confirmed build, install and launch all work on the iPhone 13 with the free team
why: the whole delivery path is now proven before any feature code depends on it
evidence: BUILD SUCCEEDED; devicectl install ok; process launch ok

decision: split the contract into four smaller units on flash-worker after the first owner produced nothing
why: the first delegate's model hit three consecutive length-stops on a large single-shot generation; smaller outputs and a different model is the fix
evidence: agent ContractOwner failed, exit 1, 12m38s, no files written

decision: all eight engine tests passed on the first run
why: the four slices compiled together with no interface drift because the declarations were copied from the frozen spec
evidence: commit fba7114, xcodebuild test: TEST SUCCEEDED

decision: mutation-checked the suite by changing the default gentle delay from 5 to 10 seconds
why: a suite where everything passes first time deserves a check that it can fail, otherwise the observation method is suspect
evidence: 6 of 8 tests red; green again after git checkout

decision: dropped a duration property that was going on the SampleSource protocol extension
why: protocol extension members dispatch statically, so reading it through an existential would have silently returned the default instead of the real value
result: removed before any code was written

decision: adopted the QA acceptance checklist and PRD v0.2 as the authority and respecified the log schema, scenarios and coordinator
why: the checklist arrived mid-build and conflicts with the v1 schema: it wants ts in milliseconds, snake_case keys present on every line, near/no_person/calibration_done vocabulary, seven screenshots and seven scenarios
result: v2 wave dispatched over four files

decision: the whole app compiled and all ten tests passed on one simulator run
why: the four v2 slices were written against the frozen specs, so they linked with no interface drift and no repair round
evidence: commit a364e23, xcodebuild test: TEST SUCCEEDED

decision: ran every scripted scenario through the simulator and checked each log with a script instead of eyeballing it
why: the acceptance criteria are timing deltas and multi-number consistency, which a hand check reads wrong; the script re-runs in seconds
result: AC1-AC7, AC11, AC12 VERIFIED; P1 VERIFIED on every run

decision: got AC6 to a zero-second delta on all five numbers in every scenario
why: the checker recomputes the statistics from the sample lines with its own code, so agreement means the summary really is derivable from the log

decision: found that nothing started the flow in a scripted run and added autoStartIfSimulating
why: the app sat on the home screen and produced one log line; the spec never said who kicks off a scripted run, so this was my omission
evidence: commit cf7f0f7, 374-line session log after the fix

decision: made a scripted run visit the settings screen after the summary
why: QA precondition P2 wants a screenshot of every key screen, and a scripted run never opened settings, so that one could never be captured
result: built; screenshot itself still blocked on the locked device

decision: could not launch on the iPhone 13 because the device is locked
why: devicectl refuses to launch into a locked device and there is no programmatic unlock, so screenshots and the heat/battery measurement need the owner
result: open, needs Link to unlock the phone

decision: screenshots verified in the simulator after relaxing the window lookup
why: the capture demanded a foregroundActive scene with a key window; falling back to the foremost scene's first window is what a headless simulator offers, and the same fallback is what a device gives before its first render

decision: found the round reporter failing because my own runner fed -sensitivity to the verifier instead of only to the launcher
why: a red round has to mean red code; this was a harness bug, and the two runs it tripped passed when re-checked by hand
result: runner fixed, fix is an argument-list change only

decision: had the app log its own battery level and thermal state every 10 seconds
why: AC8 wants heat and battery recorded and devicectl exposes neither, so the only source that reaches the evidence directory is the app's own log
evidence: tmp/handoff/acceptance-checklist.md AC8, scripts probe of devicectl device info details
result: dispatched; keys become battery_level and thermal_state on every line

decision: the phone was unlocked and the app launched on it
why: screenshots and the ARKit path can only be observed on hardware
result: device run reached the summary; installed build predates the settings-visit change

decision: ran the whole scenario round to a clean pass in the simulator
why: the earlier round was red only because my runner mis-fed an argument; with that fixed every scenario including the three sensitivity variants is green in one reproducible command

decision: five scenarios passed on the real iPhone 13 while it was unlocked
why: hardware is the only place the ARKit path and really-rendered screenshots can be observed, and the app logged battery level and thermal state there
result: VERIFIED on hardware; the phone re-locked before the remaining scenarios and the 30-minute run
